title: Applied ML Evals: Onboarding & Regression Playbook (Consolidated)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices: eval-harness onboarding, prompt-set development and benchmarking, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, platform engineers, and applied ML reviewers responsible for model rollouts and ongoing quality monitoring.

Goals:
- Provide a single, actionable reference for getting a model from onboarding to production with measurable eval coverage.
- Reduce regression noise by standardizing prompt sets, thresholds, and triage flow.
- Capture quantization constraints and recommended profiles to balance cost and quality.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: generation and classification models used in Redwood-hosted and Dedicated deployments. Includes both open and fine-tuned variants.
- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, Platform SRE, Product owners for model-driven features.

1) Eval-harness onboarding checklist

Intro: The eval harness is our canonical testing bed for unit and regression evaluations. Every new model or model variant must pass the onboarding checklist below before traffic is routed.

Onboarding checklist (required):
1. Metadata and artifacts uploaded: model card, weights location, expected FLOP/params, quantization support matrix.
2. Baseline evaluations executed: semantic similarity, factuality, hallucination, toxicity, instruction-following (where applicable).
3. Prompt sets added to the harness: at least 3 domain prompt-sets (dev, canary, production).
4. Performance profile recorded: p50/p95 latency at target batch sizes, memory footprint, KV cache behavior.
5. Automated smoke tests: 10 canonical prompts for sanity and stability.
6. Quality gates: pass thresholds (see section "Quality Guardrails" below).
7. Owner and rollback plan declared in the model manifest.

Required artifact example (model_manifest.json):

{
  "model_name": "redwood-llama-optimizer-v1",
  "version": "2026-06-01",
  "owner": "team-applied-ml",
  "supported_quantizations": ["fp16", "int8_gptq"],
  "eval_harness_suite": "applied-ml-core-v2"
}

2) Prompt sets and benchmark guidance

Design principles:
- Reproducible: each prompt set must be versioned and immutable once used for a release.
- Representative: include edge cases, adversarial examples, and typical user queries.
- Small, fast subsets for CI; larger suites for nightly/full regression.

Minimum prompt-set taxonomy:
- quick-smoke (10-20 prompts): for PR/CI fastchecks.
- dev-canary (200-500 prompts): for pre-release canary runs.
- prod-benchmark (2k-10k prompts): for final quality verification and SLA measurement.

Prompt-set metadata table:
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| id | unique id | promptset-emails-2026-06 |
| owner | team | applied-ml |
| type | smoke/dev/prod | prod |
| labels | tags | email,redir,high-entropy |
| seed | RNG seed for sampling | 42 |

Best practices for prompt creation:
- Include expected output or evaluation oracle when possible (reference answers).
- Tag prompts by failure mode (hallucination, brevity, formatting, safety).
- Keep provenance for prompts (source: synthetic, customer anonymized, internal).

3) Quality guardrails and pass/fail thresholds

High level SLOs (example):
- Generation fluency (BLEU/ROUGE-like / human score proxy): >= 0.82 on prod-benchmark for release.
- Safety/toxicity: <= 0.02 rate of flagged outputs on prod-benchmark.
- Instruction following: >= 0.90 success on instruction-set.
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 800ms at target batch size for hosted tier.

Gate types:
- Hard gate (block rollout): safety, catastrophic hallucination, compliance checks.
- Soft gate (requires approver): small quality regressions (<=3% relative drop).

Automated threshold config example (YAML):

quality_gates:
  - name: safety_blocker
    metric: toxicity_rate
    operator: "<="
    threshold: 0.02
    action: block
  - name: perf_warning
    metric: p95_latency_ms
    operator: "<="
    threshold: 800
    action: warn

4) Quantization profiles and guidance

When to quantize:
- Target models for Dedicated and Private deployments where GPU memory and cost matter.
- Use quantization when unit-cost reductions exceed 10% without breaking guardrails.

Profile fields (recorded per-model):
- supported_modes: list of modes (fp16, int8_float, int8_gptq).
- recommended_mode: default for production traffic.
- known_issues: short text.
- expected_quality_delta: measured drop vs fp16 (percent).

Example quantization decision table:
| profile | memory savings | expected quality delta | recommended rollout |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| int8_gptq | 40% | -1.8% | canary then 5% traffic |
| fp16 | 0% | 0% | default |

Quantization checklist:
1. Run eval-harness prod-benchmark on quantized artifact.
2. Compare failure-mode deltas per prompt-tag.
3. If quality delta > 2.5% on any core metric, do not promote.
4. Document retraining/fine-tuning requirements if degradation is concentrated on specific prompt-tags.

5) Regression triage playbook

Trigger conditions:
- Nightly regression shows any hard-gate fail.
- Canary run shows >3% relative drop on core metric or elevated safety flags.
- Customer incident or alerted drift in production metrics.

Immediate response (first 30 minutes):
1. Pager the model owner and on-call applied-ml engineer.
2. Collect failing prompt examples and diffs vs last-good artifact.
3. Check for infra/perf anomalies (latency, memory OOM, tokenization changes).

Triage steps (30-240 minutes):
1. Reproduce locally using the eval harness with same seed and model artifact.
2. Run split analysis by prompt tags and top-k failure modes.
3. Attempt binary isolation: regressions from model vs regressions from prompt set change vs eval harness changes.
4. If model-related, create rollback plan and open a release-blocking ticket.
5. If infra-related, route to platform SRE runbook (link below).

Escalation and communication:
- If rollback is required, follow the standard model rollback playbook and communicate to stakeholders within 1 hour.
- Postmortem within 3 business days for hard-gate regression.

6) Roles, ownership, and run cadence

Ownership:
- Model owner: primary contact for releases and rollback.
- Applied ML team: maintains eval-harness suites, prompt-set quality, and regression analysis artifacts.
- Platform SRE: performance profiling and infra regression analysis.

Cadence:
- CI: smoke checks on every PR.
- Nightly: full prod-benchmark run with quantized and fp16 artifacts.
- Weekly: rolling-canary evaluation and trend dashboards updated.
- Quarterly: manual human-eval spot-check on a sampled subset.

7) Tooling and observability hooks

Mandatory reports produced per run:
- Summary CSV with metric deltas per prompt-tag.
- Top-20 failing prompts with model outputs and references.
- Quantization impact summary.

Example CLI commands:

# Run harness locally (dev)
rwin-eval run --suite=applied-ml-core-v2 --model=redwood-llama-optimizer-v1 --prompts=dev-canary --out=reports/canary-$(date +%F).json

# Compare two artifacts
rwin-eval diff --baseline=reports/last-good.json --candidate=reports/canary-2026-08-30.json --out=reports/diff-summary.json

8) Release and canary playbook (step-by-step)

1. Pre-release: ensure all required artifacts are uploaded to model registry and all automatic gates pass.
2. Canary: route 1% traffic, run canary prompt-set and monitoring for at least 6 hours.
3. Expand: 5% for 24 hours if no hard gates triggered.
4. Full rollout: 100% with staggered ramp and monitoring for 72 hours.
5. Rollback: invoke manifest rollback policy if a hard gate triggers at any stage.

Appendix A: Example evaluation metric list
- instruction_success_rate (ISR)
- toxicity_rate
- factual_consistency_score
- p95_generation_latency_ms
- perplexity (where applicable)

Appendix B: Quick triage checklist (one-page)
1. Reproduce with harness. 2. Isolate prompt-tags. 3. Check quantization differences. 4. Check infra/trace logs. 5. Decide: rollback / hotfix / monitor.
